cost_of_waiting.formula: booked visits a week x (current no-show rate - target rate) x open weeks a year x average visit value

input_sources.booked_visits_per_week: Operations director, discovery call 2026-10-14 (from their booking reports)
input_sources.no_show_rate: Operations director, discovery call 2026-10-14 (from their booking reports)

assumptions: Every visit above the target rate is lost revenue at the average visit value (the buyer's figure).
50 open weeks a year (the buyer's figure).
Volume stays at today's 1,900 booked visits a week; the seventh clinic is not counted.
A month is one twelfth of the year.

assumptions: A booking or moving call takes as long as any other call, so 60% of calls is counted as 60% of phone hours.

deck.name: The goal you gave us
deck.headline: Quellbrook's target: no-shows under 5% at all 6 clinics before March
deck.body: Your words: "I want no-shows under 5% across the group before our seventh clinic opens in March." Today: about 9.5% of 1,900 booked visits a week.
deck.source_line: Your words and figures, operations director, discovery call 2026-10-14 (N2)
deck.notes: Open with their goal, not with us. Read their sentence back word for word and let them correct it. The target and the date are theirs; the current rate comes from their booking reports. Ask the operations director: is under five percent the number the board will judge this on, or is there a revenue figure behind it? Ask the practice manager what a good Monday would look like. If they change the target, update slide three before the meeting ends. Keep this slide up for under a minute and do not mention plans or prices.

deck.name: What stands in the way
deck.headline: Three things keep the no-show rate near one in ten
deck.body: 1. Reminders from a shared number that patients ignore. 2. Six separate calendars, so nobody sees a free slot nearby. 3. Moving a visit takes a phone call to the front desk.
deck.source_line: Your words, discovery calls 2026-10-14 and 2026-10-21 (N6, N3, N4)
deck.notes: Each blocker is in their own words: the practice manager said the old reminders came from a shared number and patients ignored them; the operations director said nobody can see a free slot at the clinic down the road; and the front desk spends half the morning on the phone moving appointments. Ask which of the three hurts most. Keep the numbers, because slides five and six take them in the same order.

deck.name: The price of waiting
deck.headline: Each month without a fix costs about $30,000 in missed visits
deck.body: 1,900 visits a week x 4.5 points above target x 50 weeks x $85 = about $360,000 a year. Estimate from your numbers.
deck.source_line: Your figures, operations director, discovery call 2026-10-14
deck.notes: Walk the math slowly; every input is theirs. The gap is the distance from today's rate to their own target, not to zero, so the number is conservative. About 4,275 visits a year sit above the target, worth about $363,375 at their average visit value, rounded down to $360,000. After this month, three full months, December to February, remain before the March opening; at this rate that is about $90,000. Ask: does this match what you see in the books? Call it an estimate.

deck.name: Someone who got there
deck.headline: A four-clinic physio group went from 11% to 4.8% no-shows
deck.body: Tarnwick Physio, Jan to Jun 2026. Before: reminders by phone from the front desk, four separate clinic calendars. Change: two-way SMS reminders and one group calendar. After: 4.8% no-shows by June 2026.
deck.source_line: Tarnwick Physio case study, published 2026-07-15, period Jan to Jun 2026 (P1)
deck.notes: Tarnwick is the closest customer we have: physiotherapy, 4 clinics against Quellbrook's 6, and they agreed to be named. Tell it in order: what they had, what they switched on, and the rate six months later, which is 56.4 percent fewer no-shows. It is one customer, so say one customer. Ask: which part of their before looks most like Quellbrook today? Offer a reference call if they want one.

deck.name: Blocker 1, removed
deck.headline: Blocker 1: reminders that come from your clinic and can be answered
deck.body: Two-way SMS reminders go out under each clinic's own name; patients reply to confirm or cancel (P13). This is what Tarnwick switched on before no-shows fell to 4.8% (P1).
deck.source_line: Reminders page, example.com/features/reminders/ (P13); Tarnwick Physio, Jan to Jun 2026 (P1)
deck.notes: This answers blocker one. The difference from what they had: the reminder comes from the clinic the patient knows, not a shared number, and the patient can answer it. Show a reminder on a phone if the demo screen is ready. Tarnwick's case study names two changes, reminders and one calendar, so do not credit the whole drop to reminders. Ask the practice manager how many hours before a visit their patients should hear from them, and note the answer for the pilot setup.

deck.name: Blockers 2 and 3, removed
deck.headline: Blockers 2 and 3: one calendar for six clinics, and rebooking online
deck.body: 2. Every front desk sees and books open slots at all six clinics (P14). 3. Patients move or cancel online at any hour (P15). Across 310 clinic accounts, 62% of bookings were online, 41% after hours (P2).
deck.source_line: Multi-location page (P14); online booking page (P15); product data, 310 clinic accounts, Jul to Sep 2026 (P2)
deck.notes: Blocker two: the group calendar lets the front desk at one clinic offer a free slot at another, which the operations director asked for directly. Blocker three: patients move or cancel from the link in the reminder, so the call to the front desk is not needed. The booking figures are product data across clinic accounts last quarter, not a promise for Quellbrook. Ask the practice manager: which calls would you most like to stop taking?

deck.name: Next to the alternative
deck.headline: Competitor A replaces your whole system; we fix no-shows inside it
deck.body: They lead with all-in-one notes, billing and scheduling, live in 6 to 8 weeks. We run beside your practice software (P12): median 9 days to live (P10). Pick them if you want to replace notes and billing too.
deck.source_line: Their Google and Meta ads and home page, seen 2026-10-27; integrations page (P12); onboarding report, 48 migrations, 2026 (P10)
deck.notes: Every line about them quotes their own material: 4 Google ads (3 with text), 3 active Meta ads and their home page, read on 2026-10-27. Their 5,000 practices figure is their own claim; if it comes up, attribute it to them. Nothing we read from them mentions no-shows; that sits in the report, not on this slide. The last line names who should pick them: a group replacing notes and billing at the same time. Ask: is replacing the whole system on the table for you?

deck.name: Open questions
deck.headline: Practitioners, moving your data, and why add another tool
deck.body: Practitioners keep their own calendars through two-way sync (P11). We move your appointments for you: median 9 days to live (P10). It runs beside your practice software; notes and billing stay where they are (P12).
deck.source_line: Calendar sync page (P11); onboarding report, Jan to Sep 2026 (P10); integrations page (P12)
deck.notes: These three came up on the discovery calls: the clinical lead said practitioners won't change how they manage their diaries, the operations director said moving five years of appointments sounds risky, and asked why add another tool when they already pay for practice software. Answer each in one breath, then ask which one is still open. Price goes in the follow-up after the decision, not on this slide.

deck.name: The decision we ask for
deck.headline: Agree today: a 4-week pilot at 2 clinics from 2026-11-16
deck.body: We set up reminders and the group calendar; your practice managers run them day to day. On 2026-12-14 we read each clinic's no-show rate against today's 9.5%.
deck.source_line: Pilot terms: our pilot offer; baseline: your figures, discovery call 2026-10-14
deck.notes: Ask for one decision: which 2 clinics start on 2026-11-16. Our side: our onboarding lead does the setup and runs one 60-minute session per clinic. Their side: the practice managers run it and send the clinic list. On 2026-12-14 both sides read the same measure they chose on slide one. Agree who sends the list and by when, offer the Tarnwick reference call, and send pricing in the follow-up email.
